items.title: 3 US Dividend Stocks Offering Defensive Cash Flow Right Now
items.summary: Interest rates are rising, inflation is stubborn, and growth stocks are feeling the pinch. That mix is pushing more investors toward US defensive, dividend-paying value stocks that may hold up better when money gets more expensive and cash flow matters more than hype. This article walks through three stocks exposed to the latest Federal Reserve moves and inflation pressures and explains why each could deserve a closer look in the current environment. items.title: How Will General Mills Stock React To Its Upcoming Earnings?
items.summary: General Mills (NYSE:GIS) is set to report its earnings on Tuesday, September 23, 2026. The company has $19 billion in current market capitalization. Revenue over the last twelve months was $18 billion, and it was operationally profitable with $2.7 billion in operating profits. While a lot will depend on how results stack up against consensus and expectations, understanding historical patterns might just turn the odds in your favor if you are an event-driven trader.

items.title: Hershey’s Dividend Is Finally Growing Again After a Nearly 2-Year Freeze
items.summary: Hershey froze its quarterly dividend for five straight cycles, and shareholders who only watched the yield number missed the warning buried in the income statement. Now that the payment is moving again, the real question is whether this resumption signals a genuine turn or just a temporary reprieve.
